findings.title: A rejected device is cached and bypasses the limit on retry
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` adds the device ID to the local cache before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` determines whether it may be admitted. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the first authentication fails, but the cache entry remains. A retry with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` on that server returns early at line 83 without consulting the store, so `Authenticate` grants anonymous access for roughly the cache TTL. Move cache insertion until after a successful store operation, or remove the entry on every store error.

findings.title: The count-then-insert limit check is not atomic
findings.body: The active-device count is queried in one database session and the later upsert is performed in another, with no transaction or locking between them. Concurrent requests with different device IDs can all observe a count below `deviceLimit` and each insert successfully, permanently exceeding the configured limit for the 30-day window. The per-process local cache does not prevent this across simultaneous requests or Grafana instances. Admission needs an atomic/serialized database operation, and a concurrent test should cover the limit boundary.

findings.title: The new anonymous device-limit setting is undocumented
findings.body: `auth.anonymous.device_limit` is parsed here, but no defaults/configuration documentation file is updated in this PR. Administrators therefore have no discoverable configuration key or explanation that zero disables the limit and that the cap applies to devices active in the last 30 days.
